content:
Hello Thanks again for your helpful reply. I have an admission to make. I asked AI for help, too. Its reply was, Thunderbird for Android (based on K-9 Mail) does not support creating new IMAP folders from within the app. You cannot create a Sent folder directly in the app. What to do instead Create the Sent folder on the server (if it doesn’t already exist) Log in to your email provider’s webmail (e.g., Gmail, Outlook.com, your domain’s webmail, etc.). Create a folder named Sent, Sent Items, or whatever your provider uses. Most providers already have one by default. Refresh the folder list in Thunderbird for Android Open the side menu (☰ top left). Select your account. Tap Manage folders (near the bottom). Tap the three-dot menu (⋮) → Refresh folders (or “Refresh folder list”). Assign the special “Sent” role Go to Settings → tap your account → Folders (or look under Manage folders / special folders). Find Sent folder. Change it from Automatic (None) to the actual Sent folder on the server (e.g., “Sent” or “Sent Items”). Use the back button to save (there is often no explicit OK button). Enable uploading of sent messages Settings → your account → Sending mail. Turn on Upload sent messages (or “Upload sent messages to Sent folder after sending”). Make the folder visible and sync In Manage folders, tap the Sent folder. Enable Sync (and optionally Push/Notifications if you want). Make sure “Show only subscribed folders” is not hiding it. After these steps, the Sent folder should appear in the folder list alongside Inbox and Outbox, and copies of messages you send from the app will be saved there. Notes Outbox is a local folder used for messages waiting to be sent. If you only see Inbox + Outbox, it usually means special folders have not been mapped yet or the server folders haven’t been refreshed/subscribed. Folder creation, renaming, and deletion are currently only possible via webmail or another email client. There is an open feature request for this on Mozilla Connect if you’d like to vote for it.
